body.statement: Under the stated recursive semi-Markovian, proxy-intervention, and positive-compatible semantic scope, for every \(A\subseteq V^{-}\), the causal target \(Q_s=Q[\{s\}]=P(s\mid\operatorname{do}(V\setminus\{s\}))\) is identifiable from \(Q[V\setminus A]=P(V\setminus A\mid\operatorname{do}(A))\) if and only if the induced graph \(G[V\setminus A]\) contains no member of \(\mathsf{Hdg}(G,s)\). Equivalently, \(A\cap(F\setminus\{s\})\neq\varnothing\) for every \(F\in\mathsf{Hdg}(G,s)\); because \(V\) is finite, this is further equivalent to \(A\cap R\neq\varnothing\) for every \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\).

source.locator: Definition 1 and Equation (2)/\(\operatorname{ID}_1(S)\), pp. 3--5; Definition 2 and the no-hedge characterization, pp. 5--6; Lemma 3 and its proof, pp. 32--33
source.verbatim_statement: A set \(A\) is a member of \(\operatorname{ID}_1(S)\) if and only if \(A\cap S=\varnothing\) and there is no hedge formed for \(Q[S]\) in \(G_{[V\setminus A]}\).

upstream.citation: Ilya Shpitser and Judea Pearl (2006), ``Identification of Joint Interventional Distributions in Recursive Semi-Markovian Causal Models,'' Proceedings of AAAI, 1219--1226.

attestation.note: Directly checked against the published JMLR PDF. The displayed sentence is transcribed from the no-hedge characterization; the node specializes it to the singleton target and records Lemma 3's hedge-hitting formulation. The final minimal-clutter equivalence removes redundant supersets in the finite hedge family.
